A1.justification: Despite the changed title, both PDFs describe the same CLIP-ViT layer-selection and feature-fusion study. The text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original layer-wise training experiments, data/model scaling evaluations, fusion comparisons, and qualitative cases in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds a 7B fusion comparison in Table 11. Its separately attributed Instruction-Guided Fusion results do not negate the original empirical results.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same LRS grouping, CLIP-ViT backbone, and feature concatenation through the connector, including the preferred layers {23,18,3}. Revised explanations and testing fusion at 7B do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: The training mixtures and evaluated task coverage remain the same. Table 11 uses benchmarks already evaluated in v1; the abstract's new '60+ tasks' wording describes existing subtasks rather than newly introduced coverage.

E2.justification: Table 11 adds Instruction-Guided Fusion as a reported comparator, explicitly borrowing its results from Li et al. The original DC-STI, DC-SCI, DC-DCI, and MMFuser comparisons remain in appendix Table 8; the shortened main Table 3 does not remove them.

E3.justification: V1 already studies individual visual layers with 7B LLMs; v2 additionally evaluates feature fusion at that scale in Table 11, stating that DenseConnector and MMFuser were retrained under the same settings. The original experiments retain their training recipe, data scales, and evaluation metrics.

E4.justification: V2 adds an aggregate analysis of the proportion of MME/SEEDBench subtasks best handled by the penultimate layer across data and model scales (Figure 5). Existing layer-combination ablations, training-free layer replacement, and four qualitative cases are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The additional results retain the existing point-score reporting practice.

E6.justification: The matched original result tables have identical entries, including v1 Table 3 relocated to v2 Table 8. New Table 11 reports 7B fusion results, such as 67.4 versus 65.1 on MMBench and 325 versus 320 on OCRBench against its 7B baseline. These are newly reported comparisons, not improvements over v1 under unchanged conditions.

T1.justification: The LRS mathematics moves from Section 3.3 to Appendix A.1 without substantive alteration, and the fusion concatenation equation is retained. The condensed model formulation changes exposition rather than mathematical assumptions or results; neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: Both versions claim similarity-based layer grouping, task-dependent advantages of shallower layers, persistence across data/model scales, and effective lightweight fusion. The new title and revised abstract emphasize these retained contributions without materially redefining them.

C2.justification: V2 adds explicit limitations concerning larger LLMs, alternative visual backbones, internal fusion, and connector architectures. It also adds interpretation of cognitive-task performance and refines the OCR fusion explanation from a general shallow-feature disadvantage to the weakness of layer 1 relative to layer 3.

D1.justification: V2 supplies a code repository link and identifies CC3M as the source of the existing 558K pretraining data. Most implementation information, including learning rates, batch sizes, hardware, training times, dataset mixtures, and evaluation tools, is retained.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially refocused on visual layer selection. New Appendix C.2 develops paper-by-paper novelty comparisons with LLaVA, DenseConnector, MMFuser, and Instruction-Guided Fusion. Additional positioning includes Lin et al. on internal fusion and Sun et al. on layer representation structure, while generic background material is reduced.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. Sections 4–5 are reorganized around deep-to-deep and deep-to-shallower comparisons, mathematical and fusion details move into reorganized appendices, and limitations, acknowledgements, and an ethics statement are added.

P2.justification: V2 substantially reformats and redistributes the displays: it shortens main Table 3 while retaining the full comparison as appendix Table 8, adds Tables 11–12 and Figure 5, and replaces the fusion-method radar with a layer-combination radar. Figure 3 uses indexed task labels linked to Table 12, and captions and page layout change throughout.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens the fusion evidence with a new 7B comparison, including DenseConnector and MMFuser retrained under common settings (Table 11). Explicit applicability limitations and code access information improve transparency. These are limited gains: the core experiments remain unchanged, and the borrowed Instruction-Guided Fusion results do not establish a fully controlled comparison.
